source_text: Dialexis Montanistae et orthodoxi Μοντανιστοῦ καὶ Ὀρθοδόξου διάλεξις. Μοντανιστὴς εἶπεν· Ἡμεῖς τῷ ἁγίῳ Παύλῳ πειθόμενοι Μοντανὸν ἐδεξάμεθα, ὡς ἔχοντα τὸ τέλειον τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, τουτέστιν τὸν παράκλητον. Αὐτὸς γὰρ εἶπεν Παῦλος· Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται· καί· ἐκ μέρους γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν. 450 Ὀρθόδοξος· Ἀληθεύων εἶπεν ὁ ἅγιος Παῦλος ἢ ψευδόμενος; {Μ.} Ἀληθεύων. {Ο.} Κατήργηται οὖν τὰ τοῦ ἀποστόλου; {Μ.} Μὴ γένοιτο. {Ο.} Πῶς οὖν εἶπεν· ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται, ὡς ἀληθεύων ἢ ὡς ψευδόμενος; {Μ.} Αὐτὸς εἶπεν· ἐκ μέρους γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν. {Ο.} Ἀληθῶς λέγεις, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐνόησας, ὅτι πᾶς λόγος ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ μέρος ἐστὶ τοῦ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι φανησομένου μυστηρίου. Νῦν γὰρ πιστεύομεν εἰς πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν καὶ ἅγιον πνεῦμα καὶ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις ἔχομεν· τότε δὲ ἡ γνῶσις, ὅτε πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον ὀψώμεθα. ! Ἄρτι πιστεύομεν, ὅτι αὐτὸς κύριος ἐν κελεύσματι, ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου καὶ ἐν σάλπιγγι θεοῦ καταβήσεται ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ· τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον. Τῶν οὖν πραγμάτων κατὰ πρόσωπον ὀφθέντων τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται. Οὐκέτι γὰρ ἀπὸ λόγων ἔχομεν τὴν πίστιν, ἀλλὰ ἀπ' αὐτῆς τῆς θέας, καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται. {Μ.} Καταργηθήσεται οὖν καὶ ἡ πίστις; {Ο.} Καταργηθήσεται. Ἀντὶ τοῦ παύεται. Ἀμέλει αὐτῆς ὅλης τῆς περικοπῆς μνησθῶμεν τῇ συνέσει τοῦ πνεύματος. Λέγει δὲ οὕτως· ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε πίπτει· εἴτε δὲ προφητεία, καταργηθήσεται. Ἐκ μέρους γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν· ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται. Ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος, ὡς νήπιος ἐλάλουν, ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος· ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ, κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου. Βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι δι' ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον· ἄρτι γιγνώσκωμεν ἐκ μέρους, τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην. Ὁρᾶς, ὅτι καταργηθήσεται ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον· ὅ ἐστι τί; Παρόντων τῶν πιστευομένων παύ 451 σεται ἡ πίστις. Οὐκέτι γὰρ πιστεύομεν, ἀλλ' ὁρῶμεν. Πίστις δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστι πίστις. Ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τις, τί καὶ πιστεύει; καὶ τοῦτό ἐστι· βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι δι' ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον. Τότε, πότε; ∆ῆλον, ὅτε τὸ τέλος. {Μ.} Ἰδοὺ οὖν ἦλθεν Μοντανὸς ὁ παράκλητος καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ τέλειον. {Ο.} Τὸ τέλειον ὅταν ἔλθῃ, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται ἢ οὔ; {Μ.} Οὕτως γέγραπται. {Ο.} Ὁρῶμεν δέ, ὅτι Μοντανὸς καταργεῖται ἕως σήμερον· τὰ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου Παύλου αὔξουσιν. {Μ.} Καί τοι γε ὑμεῖς τὰ Παύλου καταργεῖτε λέγοντος μετὰ Χριστὸν μὴ εἶναι προφήτας. {Ο.} Πλανᾶσθε, μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ ἃ διδάσκει ἡ ἐκκλησία. Ἡμεῖς γὰρ ἴσμεν, ὅτι καὶ μετὰ Χριστὸν προφῆται. Αὐτὸς γὰρ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν, ὅτι· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστελῶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν. Καὶ Παῦλος λέγει· Ζηλοῦτε τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα, μᾶλλον δέ, ἵνα προφητεύητε. Καὶ πάλιν λέγει· Ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλῶσιν, εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι, οὐκ ἐροῦσιν, ὅτι μαίνεσθε; ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύσωσιν, εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης, ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων, τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ καὶ φανερὰ γίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων, καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ θεῷ ἀπαγγέλλων, ὅτι ὄντως Θεὸς ἐστὶν ἐν ἡμῖν. {Μ.} Πῶς οὖν ὑμεῖς λέγετε, ὅτι μετὰ Χριστὸν οὐκ ἐγένετό τις προφήτης; {Ο.} Ἡμεῖς καὶ μετὰ Χριστὸν ὁμολογοῦμεν γεγενῆσθαι προφήτας καὶ 1 αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἔχειν καὶ τῆς προφητείας 452 τὸ χάρισμα.
thought_title: The perfect is the future vision, not Montanus
orientation: The Montanist opens the dialogue by claiming that Paul's promise of 'the perfect' was fulfilled in Montanus as the Advocate, and the Orthodox Christian begins his reply.
pass_a_gloss: Dialogue of a Montanist and an Orthodox Christian. The Montanist said: We, obeying holy Paul, received Montanus, as having the perfect of the Holy Spirit, that is, the Advocate. For Paul himself said: But when the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished; and: we know in part and we prophesy in part. Orthodox: Did holy Paul speak truthfully or falsely? M. Truthfully. O. Have the things of the apostle then been abolished? M. May it not be. O. How then did he say: but when the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished, as speaking truthfully or as speaking falsely? M. He himself said: we know in part and we prophesy in part. O. You speak truly, but you did not understand, that every word in this age is a part of the mystery that will be revealed in the age to come. For now we believe in Father and Son and Holy Spirit and we have them in words; but then there is knowledge, when we see face to face. Now we believe, that the Lord himself with a shout, with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God will come down from heaven; but then face to face. When therefore the realities are seen face to face, what is partial will be abolished. For no longer do we have faith from words, but from the sight itself, and this is what is partial will be abolished. M. Will faith then also be abolished? O. It will be abolished. That is, it ceases. Indeed let us recall the whole passage with the understanding of the Spirit. He speaks thus: love never falls; but if there are prophecies, they will be abolished. For we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I abolished the things of the child. For we see now through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face; now we know in part, but then I will know fully even as I have been fully known. Do you see, that it will be abolished for the better; which is what? When the things believed are present, faith will cease. For no longer do we believe, but we see. And faith that is seen is not faith. For what someone sees, why does he also believe? And this is it: for we see now through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face. Then, when? Clearly, when the end comes. M. Behold then Montanus the Advocate came and gave us the perfect. O. When the perfect comes, will what is partial be abolished or not? M. So it is written. O. But we see, that Montanus is abolished until today; but the things of holy Paul increase. M. And yet you abolish the things of Paul, who says that after Christ there are no prophets. O. You are deceived, not knowing the scriptures nor what the church teaches. For we know, that there are prophets also after Christ. For Jesus himself said, that: Behold I send to you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues. And Paul says: Desire earnestly the greater gifts, but rather, that you may prophesy. And again he says: If therefore the whole church comes together in the same place and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say, that you are mad? But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is examined by all, the hidden things of his heart also become manifest by all, and so falling on his face he will worship God declaring, that truly God is in you. M. How then do you say, that after Christ no prophet arose? O. We confess that prophets arose also after Christ and that the apostles themselves also had the gift of prophecy.

choices.why: The glossary fixes 'Advocate' for the Holy Spirit, and the Montanist uses the same term for Montanus; keeping one English word preserves the contested identification.
The glossary fixes 'the perfect' for the state Paul says will come; the whole argument turns on what this phrase names.
The glossary fixes 'what is partial' for the present knowledge and prophecy that will cease; the phrase recurs throughout the section.
The verb is the hinge of the argument; 'abolished' keeps the strong sense of being done away with, and the same rendering is used for the Montanist's claim that Montanus is abolished.
The Orthodox speaker contrasts present faith through words with the future direct vision; the literal phrase is the key to his interpretation of 'the perfect'.
The Orthodox speaker quotes Paul's mirror-and-riddle image to explain present partial knowledge; 'riddle' keeps the obscurity of the present state.

pass_b_english: The Montanist said: "We obey Saint Paul, and that is why we accepted Montanus, because he had the perfect of the Holy Spirit—that is, the Advocate. For Paul himself said: 'When the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished' (1 Corinthians 13:10), and: 'We know in part and we prophesy in part' (1 Corinthians 13:9)."
The Orthodox Christian said: "Did Saint Paul speak the truth, or did he speak falsely?"
The Montanist said: "He spoke the truth."
The Orthodox Christian said: "Then have the apostle's words been abolished?"
The Orthodox Christian said: "Then how did he say, 'When the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished'—as one speaking the truth, or as one speaking falsely?"
The Montanist said: "He himself said: 'We know in part and we prophesy in part.'"

The Orthodox Christian said: "You speak truly, but you have not understood that every word in this age is a part of the mystery that will be revealed in the age to come. For now we believe in Father and Son and Holy Spirit, and we have them in words; but then there will be knowledge, when we see face to face. Now we believe that the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God; but then, face to face. So when the realities themselves are seen face to face, what is partial will be abolished. For no longer will we have faith from words, but from the sight itself—and this is what 'what is partial will be abolished' means."
The Montanist said: "Then will faith also be abolished?"

The Orthodox Christian said: "It will be abolished—that is, it will cease. Let us recall the whole passage, with the understanding the Spirit gives. It says this: 'Love never fails; but as for prophecies, they will be abolished. For we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished. When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child; when I became a man, I did away with the things of a child. For now we see through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face; now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I have been fully known' (1 Corinthians 13:8-12). Do you see that it will be abolished for the better? What does that mean? When the things we believe are present, faith will cease. For no longer do we believe, but we see. And faith that is seen is not faith. For what someone sees, why does he still believe? And this is what it means: 'For now we see through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face.' Then—when? Clearly, when the end comes."
The Montanist said: "Look, then: Montanus the Advocate has come and given us the perfect."
The Orthodox Christian said: "When the perfect comes, will what is partial be abolished, or not?"
The Montanist said: "That is what is written."
The Orthodox Christian said: "But we see that Montanus is being abolished even to this day, while the words of Saint Paul are increasing."
The Montanist said: "And yet you abolish Paul's words when he says that after Christ there are no prophets."

The Orthodox Christian said: "You are deceived, not knowing the Scriptures or what the church teaches. For we know that there are prophets even after Christ. Jesus himself said: 'Behold, I am sending you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues' (Matthew 23:34). And Paul says: 'Earnestly desire the greater gifts, and especially that you may prophesy' (1 Corinthians 12:31 and 14:1). And again he says: 'If, then, the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds? But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is examined by all, the secrets of his heart become known, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God and declare that God is truly among you' (1 Corinthians 14:23-25)."
The Montanist said: "Then how can you say that after Christ no prophet has arisen?"
The Orthodox Christian said: "We confess that prophets have arisen even after Christ, and that the apostles themselves also have the gift of prophecy."

problems.quote: and that the apostles themselves also had the gift of prophecy
problems.source_quote: καὶ αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἔχειν καὶ τῆς προφητείας τὸ χάρισμα
problems.why: The Greek says 'that the apostles themselves also have [ἔχειν] the gift of prophecy' - present infinitive, not past 'had'. The English 'had' changes tense and misrepresents the argument. The Orthodox speaker is saying the apostles HAVE (still possess) the gift of prophecy, not that they merely had it in the past. This is a key point against the Montanist claim that the apostles lacked the full Spirit.
problems.fix: and that the apostles themselves also have the gift of prophecy
problems.ruling: ἔχειν is present infinitive 'to have'; English 'had' implies past possession, misrepresenting the Orthodox argument.

problems.why: The Greek text quotes ζηλοῦτε τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα, μᾶλλον δέ, ἵνα προφητεύητε. This combines 1 Cor 12:31 (ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα) with 14:1 (ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε). The citation '1 Corinthians 12:31' alone is incomplete/misleading since the full quotation spans verses and the μᾶλλον δέ clause is from 14:1.
problems.ruling: μᾶλλον δέ, ἵνα προφητεύητε is from 1 Cor 14:1, not 12:31; citation is wrong, misleading reader.

last_rejected.why: Repeatedly translating καταργηθήσεται as 'abolished' is too strong; in context it means 'done away with, cease, pass away'. 'Abolished' suggests active suppression.
last_rejected.fix: Use 'pass away' or 'cease' or 'be done away with' — but the source uses καταργηθήσεται throughout, and the English does use 'cease' at 451. However 'abolished' is within normal range for καταργέω. Not reporting.
last_rejected.ruling: καταργηθήσεται means 'abolished/done away with/cease'; 'abolished' is within normal range, not misleading.
